title: Claude as an EDA Tool Wiki - Semiwiki
gist: SemiWiki publishes a vendor-neutral reference architecture for inserting Anthropic's Claude and Claude Code into semiconductor design flows as an advisory reasoning layer that never holds authority: every AI-produced RTL patch, SVA property, constraint change or triage conclusion must pass deterministic EDA tool gates before it counts. The piece's implied commercial view is that AI value in EDA accrues to whoever builds the narrow typed adapters, evidence stores and approval gates around the model, not to the model itself.

insights.claim: In a semiconductor design flow, large language models such as Claude occupy an advisory reasoning layer while compilers, simulators, formal engines and signoff tools retain sole authority for their configured task, and the human engineering layer keeps final decision authority.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: The three-layer split predicts that AI spend in EDA lands on orchestration and evidence plumbing, not on replacing licensed tool seats — EDA vendor license revenue is not the thing being disrupted first.

insights.claim: Claude is explicitly not a simulator, formal engine, synthesizer, place-and-route system, timing signoff tool, or golden reference, so it cannot substitute for any of the seat-licensed EDA products it sits beside.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Bearish framing for the 'LLMs will eat EDA tools' narrative: incumbent tool moats are described as intact by an industry-native publication.
insights.quote: It is not a simulator, formal engine, synthesizer, place-and-route system, timing signoff tool, or golden reference.
insights.locator: POSITIONING Claude is an AI reasoning

insights.claim: The governing operating rule for AI in chip design is that every model-produced diagnosis, patch, assertion, constraint or script is a hypothesis until it passes deterministic checks, which caps the achievable automation rate regardless of model quality.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Compute demand from AI-assisted design scales with verification reruns, not just inference — a tailwind for simulation and regression compute/licensing volumes.
insights.quote: Treat every Claude-produced diagnosis, patch, assertion, constraint, or script as a hypothesis that must pass deterministic checks.

insights.claim: Conversational confidence from a language model and engineering confidence are distinct quantities, and only reproducible tool results, complete artifacts and accountable review produce the latter.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A reusable filter for evaluating any vendor's 'agentic design' claims: ask what evidence artifact the agent emits, not how fluent it sounds.
insights.quote: A safe system separates conversational confidence from engineering confidence. The former is not evidence.

insights.claim: A production AI-in-EDA deployment should expose narrow typed operations such as compile_target, run_test, query_failure and fetch_report rather than unrestricted shell access, making the adapter surface the real engineering product.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Identifies the integration layer — typed EDA adapters and MCP servers — as the defensible build, a likely acquisition target for Synopsys/Cadence-class buyers.
insights.quote: An EDA adapter should expose narrow, typed operations—for example, compile_target, run_test, query_failure, or fetch_report—rather than unrestricted shell access.
insights.locator: Claude can connect to external tools

insights.claim: The recommended reference architecture inserts five stages between the engineer and the model — context gateway, agent, execution broker, evidence store and human gate — each with its own controls such as redaction, sandboxing, license limits and immutable traces.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Each stage is a product category in its own right; watch for startups selling the execution broker and evidence store rather than the model.

insights.claim: Numeric extraction from EDA reports should be done by deterministic parsers in code, with the language model reserved for interpretation, prioritization and narrative — a division that limits hallucinated metrics.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Any 'AI reads your reports' pitch that lets the model parse numbers directly is architecturally weaker than one that parses first and reasons second.
insights.quote: Use structured parsers for numbers; use Claude for interpretation, prioritization, and narrative.

insights.claim: Tool execution for AI agents in chip flows must carry wall-clock, CPU, memory, output and license limits with orphaned-job cancellation, because an unbounded agent can silently consume scarce EDA license pools.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: License consumption is an underpriced cost line in agentic-EDA business cases; ask vendors how they meter it.

insights.claim: Regression failure triage is the highest-value entry point for AI in verification because failures can be signature-normalized and duplicate-grouped before any reasoning happens, leaving the model to rank hypotheses against bounded evidence.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Verification-triage tooling is the first place AI-in-EDA revenue is likely to show up; watch DV-focused startups and EDA vendor triage add-ons.

insights.claim: AI-generated verification content should be required to produce negative and boundary scenarios, not only happy-path stimulus, and must be checked for reset semantics, sampling regions, implication choice, disable conditions, vacuity and overconstraint.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A concrete audit checklist for judging whether an 'AI writes your assertions' claim is credible or cosmetic.

insights.claim: A prompt for engineering work should be structured as an explicit task contract — role, bounded objective, allowed artifacts, allowed tools, prohibited actions, success criteria, required evidence and output schema — rather than open-ended instruction.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Transferable beyond EDA: the same contract shape is what separates deployable enterprise agents from demos.
insights.quote: Role + bounded objective + allowed artifacts + allowed tools + prohibited actions + success criteria + required evidence + output schema.

insights.claim: Model-generated RTL can compile cleanly and still be functionally wrong, non-synthesizable, timing-hostile, power-expensive or unsafe across clock and reset domains, so compile success is a worthless quality signal in silicon design.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Explains why AI code-generation productivity gains from software will not transfer one-for-one to hardware; discount vendor claims that cite compile rates.
insights.quote: Generated RTL may compile yet be functionally wrong, non-synthesizable, timing-hostile, power-expensive, or unsafe across clock/reset domains.

insights.claim: Agent behavior in engineering flows drifts with changes to the model, prompt, tool descriptions, context ordering and platform updates, which means every upstream vendor release forces a re-qualification cycle.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Recurring re-validation cost is a structural drag on enterprise AI margins and a reason regulated/hardware customers move slower than software ones.
insights.quote: Model behavior can change with model, prompt, tool descriptions, context ordering, and platform updates.

insights.claim: Large repositories and long logs dilute the relevant context, so retrieval and summarization can omit the decisive evidence in a debug problem even when the model is otherwise capable.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Retrieval quality, not raw model capability, is the binding constraint on AI debug value — favors tools with strong provenance-preserving retrieval.

insights.claim: No language model can certify silicon correctness or replace accountable engineering signoff, which permanently keeps a human liability holder in the tapeout loop.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Headcount reduction theses for verification teams should be discounted; the realistic outcome is throughput per engineer, not engineer elimination.
insights.quote: Claude cannot certify silicon correctness or replace accountable engineering signoff.

themes.theme: IP, export control and data boundaries

insights.claim: Repository and project boundaries for AI agents must be enforced at the tool layer rather than only in prompt instructions, because prompt-level restrictions are not a security control.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A fast diligence test for any agentic-AI vendor: if the guardrail lives in the system prompt, it is not a guardrail.
insights.quote: Enforce repository and project boundaries at the tool layer, not only in prompt instructions.

insights.claim: Export-control, third-party IP and clean-room requirements apply to the context retrieved into an AI agent and to its generated output, extending semiconductor trade restrictions into the AI tooling layer itself.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Cross-border AI-assisted design is a compliance surface — relevant to any chip design operation spanning US/China/Taiwan jurisdictions.

insights.claim: Unredacted PDK files, proprietary tool binaries, license credentials, secure-boot secrets, customer netlists and restricted design data are named as categorically off-limits to AI processing without explicit authorization and an approved environment.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Defines the data classes that will need on-prem or dedicated-tenancy AI deployment — an addressable market for private model hosting in semis.
insights.locator: DO NOT EXPOSE Unredacted PDK files

insights.claim: The recommended adoption path is a shadow-mode pilot scored against historical bugs, then read-only live triage, then gated tool execution, and only finally limited write assistance — with a non-AI baseline maintained throughout.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Implies multi-quarter sales cycles for agentic EDA products; revenue recognition lags announcement by design.
insights.quote: Run a shadow-mode pilot on historical bugs first.

insights.claim: The proposed success metrics for AI in verification are top-k root-cause recall, ownership accuracy, unsupported-claim rate, time to verified fix, escaped-defect rate, runs per resolved issue and override rate — none of which are model benchmark scores.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Gives investors an ROI vocabulary to press vendors on; 'benchmark performance' answers should be treated as evasion.

insights.claim: Autonomous signoff, credential access, bypass of repository controls and presenting unsupported claims as verified root cause are placed in a hard-prohibit category, while any tool execution, repo write, regression launch or constraint change is merely gated.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: The allow/gate/prohibit trichotomy is a portable policy template for deploying agents in any regulated or high-liability engineering domain.
